podcasts.title: 154. 对Dyna创始人Lindon的3小时访谈：机器人世界的迷雾、分歧与抉择，修心、《沉思录》与王阳明
podcasts.summary:
今天我们的嘉宾是一位美国连续创业者，Dyna Robotics创始人兼CEO Lindon Gao。此前，他做过两段生意，一次完整的创业。Dyna可以说是他的第四次创业了。
在硅谷，Dyna和之前来过我们节目的Pi（Physical Intelligence）的纯大脑研究路线非常不一样。相比从通用智能出发、探索机器人大脑的研究路径，
Dyna选择了一条“Product-research”的道路：以具体的工作流为最小单元，从真实任务出发，反过来驱动模型的预训练。
全球机器人行业还远远没有达到收敛的时刻。这是一条无比漫长的长跑——你看不见终点，有时候你也看不出清楚四周。每一位创业者都必须在这张尚未绘制完成的地图上，找到自己的方向，做出关键决策，并在迷途中找回自己。
而Lindon谈到，创业也是一场自我的修心。有时候，真正的转变只在一念之间。
过去，他曾要求自己做一个“不能犯错的CEO”。但后来他意识到，恰恰是这种对犯错的恐惧，让自己“为了不能犯错而做了很多错误的决策”。
直到去年底，他才刚刚渡过了这段难关。

podcasts.title: 184: 与陈哲的「具身季报26Q3」：Astra冲击后，通用模型会吃掉Robotics吗？
podcasts.summary:
2026 年 Q3，具身智能领域最有冲击力的变化，来自一个通用模型：9 月初 OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Astra 后，具身从业者们发现，Astra 不只理解任务、拆解任务，还能输出机器人末端执行器的位姿，完成了本该属于 VLA 等物理 AI 模型的部分工作，而且还做得很不错。
在部分测试中，直接把 Astra 当做策略模型（VLA、WAM 等都是机器人上的策略模型类型）的成功率已超过了一些专门为机器人任务和物理世界操作训练的具身模型。
这动摇了数字世界 AI 和物理 AI 的边界，也引发了一个灵魂拷问：
GPT、Fable 之类的通用模型是否会吃掉 Robotics？
同时已经发生的事实是：OpenAI、Anthropic、DeepSeek、Kimi 等多数通用前沿模型公司都正酝酿进入 robotics。
除了 Astra 冲击外，本期具身季报还关注以下 4 个行业进展和事件：
AMD 拟以 82 亿美元收购 World Labs
宇树 IPO 及连锁反应
有可能大幅压缩部署成本的 “上下文学习”
美国 FCC 实际禁止了新型号的中国机器人进口
对一些人来说，Astra 的变化已经撼动了独立的具身智能公司的发展叙事和估值逻辑。至少，现在到了重新思考物理 AI 与通用 AI 边界的时刻。
本期节目已发布图文版，

podcasts.title: Jensen Huang | Does AI Revenue Justify Capex, '27 AI Bottlenecks, Singularity, Open vs Closed & more
podcasts.summary:
Can AI revenues justify the spending? Jensen Huang breaks down the biggest bottlenecks heading into 2027, the path to the singularity, open vs. closed models, and why he’s 99.99% optimistic about the decade ahead.
Jensen joins Brad Gerstner and Clark Tang for their third BG2 conversation, recorded days after the Xi State Dinner, the White House Accord on superintelligence, and his receipt of the National Medal of Science. They explore why building technology responsibly also means moving fast, how power constraints could shape AI’s next phase, and whether SpaceX could help put data centers in orbit. Jensen also explains why NVIDIA sees demand extending far beyond just two AI labs.
Produced by STMNT Studios

This is one of the most exhilarating times in technology, and this challenge was yet another jaw-dropping moment.

When the details of OpenAI’s agent escape and Hugging Face hack started to emerge, it became clear that agent containment would be one of the most important priorities for any AI infra company.

There are two classes of escapes: ① "escape the network" and ② “escape the matrix” 😁, as in, break the spell of virtualization. OpenAI was the former, where an agent not supposed to have internet access… gained it by hacking another system. Genuinely astonishing and worrisome.

Through this challenge, however, we discovered something even more groundbreaking. A talented white-hat researcher, armed with a swarm of AI agents, expertise and perseverance, "pierced through" the Linux virtualization boundary that nearly every cloud sandbox provider in the world banks on today.

I'm very thankful we got the report, were able to quickly move to protect our customers, found no evidence of customer data compromise, and collaborated with many industry partners to protect the wider internet.
